title: Push a tee into a rubber holder and balance a golf ball on it
instruction: Push the tee into the rubber holder, then balance the golf ball on the tee.
context: 28.1 million Americans played golf on a course in 2024, the most since 2008 (National Golf Foundation, ngf.org, 'Golf participation growing, diversifying'). Every drive on a course or a driving range starts this way: the tee is pushed upright into the ground, or at home into a hitting mat's rubber tee holder, at driver height, then the ball is set on the tee's cup, which is only 9 mm across. A ball let go 9 mm off-centre rolls off (one of the runs shows it); a tee left leaning or too high will not hold it.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left. A black Carl's Place Rubber Tee Holder (1.5 in tall, 2 in wide at its flat rubber base; its tight bore grips a tee) stands on the bare table at x 33, y 0, stuck down with double-sided tape in a real trial. In the simulation the bore runs through to the table, so a tee pushed fully home stops with its tip on the table; if a real holder's bore is shallower the tee stands a little higher, still inside the scored range. A natural-wood Pride Professional Tee System ProLength Plus tee, 3 1/4 in (82.55 mm) long, with an 11 mm head with a shallow cup and a 4.8 mm shank, about 1.4 g, lies flat on the table along y: its tip at x 40, y -15.5, its head toward the holder. A white golf ball (45.93 g, 42.67 mm: the Rules of Golf limits) rests on the table at x 42, y -3. Both grippers start open at the ready pose. Nothing else is in the scene. Pushed fully home, the tee's top stands 44 mm (82.55 - 38.1) above the holder's top.
scoring: Read once, 3 s after the last release, from one side photo against a protractor and a ruler, with both hands at least 3 cm from the ball and the tee. 1.0: the tee stands in the holder within 5 degrees of vertical, the top of its head is 38 to 51 mm above the holder's top (Golf Guidebook gives 1.5 to 1.75 in for a driver; the range adds a quarter inch above it), and the ball rests on the tee's cup touching nothing else. 0.5: the tee stands so, but the ball is not on it. 0: anything else, including the untouched scene (tee lying flat), a tee left leaning or too high, or a hand still on the ball or the tee. The simulation reads the same checks from the end poses.
reset_notes: Pull the tee out of the holder; lay the tee and the ball back on their marks on the table. About 10 s. Nothing is used up.
fidelity: Rigid ball, tee and holder at real sizes and masses. The holder is fixed in the simulation (taped down in a real trial). Its grip is four pads on sliders, sprung against the shank (about 6 N to push a tee in): the tee stands only by that squeeze and friction. The cup is a 9.2 mm ring. Estimates: frictions, the tee's mass, the holder's 22 mm tube and 3 mm base (square in the simulation). No bounce. Left out: the rubber's give, the wood's flex.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0
